status: DRAFT. No doses. Classes, drugs, routes and attributes are proposals for CSO review; every dose is filled only by the verification phase with a quoted source.

conventions.flags: weightBasedInChildren/weightBasedInAdults mean the verified dose is expected to be weight- or weight-band-based; they carry no number. highAlert follows the ISMP high-alert medication categories. reserveAntibiotic means WHO AWaRe Reserve only.
conventions.onEmhsluDraft: Drafter's belief about the Essential Medicines and Health Supplies List for Uganda; null means unsure. Must be checked against the current EMHSLU before use.
conventions.diagnosisLinks: Decision support for browsing only, not a treatment recommendation. Links point to classes, never to a single drug.

classes.name: Penicillins
classes.note: Natural, aminopenicillins and antistaphylococcal penicillins in one class. Beta-lactam cross-reactivity is checked through the beta-lactam group.

classes.name: Penicillins with beta-lactamase inhibitor
classes.note: Piperacillin-tazobactam is WHO AWaRe Watch.

classes.name: Cephalosporins
classes.note: Parent group; choose a generation.

classes.name: Cephalosporins, third generation
classes.note: WHO AWaRe Watch. Ceftazidime is the antipseudomonal member.

classes.name: Cephalosporins, fourth generation
classes.note: WHO AWaRe Watch.

classes.name: Carbapenems
classes.note: WHO AWaRe Watch; usually restricted to microbiology or senior approval.

classes.name: Aminoglycosides
classes.note: Levels and renal function guide use.

classes.name: Fluoroquinolones
classes.note: WHO AWaRe Watch. Active against TB, so can mask it when TB is not excluded.

classes.name: Nitroimidazoles
classes.note: Anaerobic and antiprotozoal cover. Listed once here, not under antiparasitics.

classes.name: Sulfonamide combinations
classes.note: Includes co-trimoxazole preventive therapy in HIV.

classes.name: Glycopeptides
classes.note: WHO AWaRe Watch. Levels guide use.

classes.name: Other antibacterials
classes.note: Merged class: nitrofurantoin (lower urinary tract only) and chloramphenicol.

classes.name: Antituberculosis medicines
classes.note: First-line drugs and fixed-dose combinations. Drug-resistant TB regimens are programme-managed and not listed. Pyridoxine is under vitamins.

classes.name: Antimalarials
classes.note: Merged class: artemisinin-based drugs, quinine and primaquine. Primaquine needs G6PD consideration.

classes.name: Antifungals
classes.note: Merged class: azoles, polyenes and flucytosine. The two amphotericin B formulations are not interchangeable.

classes.name: Antivirals (non-HIV)
classes.note: Herpesviruses and influenza.

classes.name: Antiretrovirals
classes.note: Single agents and fixed-dose combinations in one class. Regimen choice follows the national HIV guidelines. Tenofovir disoproxil is also the hepatitis B treatment.

classes.name: Anthelmintics
classes.note: Metronidazole is under nitroimidazoles.

classes.name: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
classes.note: Aspirin is under antiplatelets.

classes.name: Opioids
classes.note: Controlled medicines. Weak and strong opioids in one class.

classes.name: Acid suppressants
classes.note: Proton pump inhibitor and H2-receptor antagonist. Ranitidine was withdrawn globally and is not listed.

classes.name: Antiemetics
classes.note: Merged class: dopamine antagonists, 5-HT3 antagonists and antihistamine antiemetics.

classes.name: Laxatives
classes.note: Lactulose is also the first-line drug in hepatic encephalopathy.

classes.name: Drugs for complications of liver disease
classes.note: Hepatic encephalopathy (rifaximin) and variceal bleeding (octreotide).

classes.name: Calcium channel blockers
classes.note: Dihydropyridines (amlodipine, nifedipine).

classes.name: Potassium-sparing diuretics
classes.note: Includes the aldosterone antagonist spironolactone.

classes.name: Beta-blockers
classes.note: Labetalol and carvedilol also block alpha receptors.

classes.name: Vasodilator and centrally acting antihypertensives
classes.note: Merged class: hydralazine and methyldopa.

classes.name: Antiarrhythmics and cardiac glycosides
classes.note: Merged class: digoxin (cardiac glycoside) and amiodarone.

classes.name: Anticoagulants
classes.note: Heparins, vitamin K antagonist and direct oral anticoagulants in one class. Vitamin K and protamine are under haemostatics.

classes.name: Vasopressors and inotropes
classes.note: Includes adrenaline for anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest.

classes.name: Inhaled corticosteroids, alone or with a long-acting beta-2 agonist
Insulins
classes.note: Short-acting, intermediate, premixed and long-acting. Choose by full name, never by abbreviation.

classes.name: Oral glucose-lowering drugs
classes.note: Merged class: metformin (biguanide) and sulfonylureas.

classes.name: Corticosteroids, systemic
classes.note: Glucocorticoids plus fludrocortisone (mineralocorticoid).

classes.name: Antiepileptics
classes.note: Aromatic agents share a hypersensitivity group.

classes.name: Benzodiazepines
classes.note: Controlled medicines.

classes.name: Antipsychotics
classes.note: First and second generation in one class.

classes.name: Antidepressants
classes.note: Tricyclic (also neuropathic pain) and SSRIs. Tricyclics are dangerous in overdose.

classes.name: Haematinics
classes.note: Iron, folic acid and vitamin B12.

classes.name: Vitamins
classes.note: Thiamine before glucose in suspected Wernicke's; pyridoxine with isoniazid.

classes.name: IV fluids and glucose
classes.note: Crystalloids, glucose solutions and albumin.

classes.name: Electrolytes
classes.note: Concentrated potassium and hypertonic saline are high-alert.

classes.name: Blood and blood components
classes.note: Supportive class, ordered through the transfusion pathway; nothing about volumes is set here.

classes.name: Antidotes and emergency reversal
classes.note: Atropine sits here and is also used for bradycardia.

classes.name: Gout treatment and prevention
classes.note: Colchicine (acute, also pericarditis) and allopurinol (urate-lowering).

classes.name: Vaccines, immunoglobulins and antivenoms
classes.note: Post-exposure prophylaxis follows the national schedule. Adrenaline must be ready before antivenom.

oral: By mouth on an empty stomach

supportive.name: IV and oral fluids
supportive.note: Volume and rate are ordered on the fluid chart, not set here.

supportive.name: Oxygen
supportive.note: Supportive item, not a drug entry. Target saturation and delivery device are prescribed separately.

supportive.name: Nutrition support
supportive.note: Diet, feeds and therapeutic milks are ordered by the nutrition team.
